dashboard.journeySubtitle: On-demand movement therapy, insights, and peer encouragement.
facts: Even 10 minutes of light movement increases blood flow to the brain, improving focus and mood.
Consistency is more important than intensity when it comes to neuroplasticity.
Movement triggers the release of BDNF, a protein that acts like fertilizer for your brain cells.
Your brain uses 20% of your body's energy. Gentle movement helps deliver oxygen efficiently.

brainFacts.0: Aerobic movement stimulates BDNF (Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor), triggering new neuronal connections and neuroplasticity.
brainFacts.1: Just 10 minutes of rhythmic movement increases dopamine levels, improving motor control and reducing tremors or stiffness.
brainFacts.2: Rhythmic movement synchronizes neural firing patterns, helping bypass damaged motor pathways in neurological conditions.
brainFacts.3: Consistent daily movement triggers neurogenesis in the hippocampus, strengthening memory and cognitive resistance.
brainFacts.4: Cross-body coordination exercises recruit both brain hemispheres, rewiring motor signals around neural lesion areas.
brainFacts.5: Rest days and gentle movement days actively consolidate neuroplastic gains made during vigorous movement sessions.
brainFacts.6: Movement releases endorphins and reduces cortisol, directly decreasing pain perception and daily symptom intensity.
